name: music_cardiac_death
outcome_definition: Cardiac death - the MUSIC study's own primary endpoint, sudden cardiac death or pump-failure death - occurring within 1461 days (4 years) of enrolment. Features are the clinical, echocardiographic, radiographic and laboratory measurements taken at enrolment, so the outcome genuinely postdates every predictor: this is prognosis over a defined horizon, not detection of disease already present. Landmark labelling: positives died of cardiac causes within the horizon; negatives were observed event-free through the full horizon; patients censored before the horizon (lost, transplanted, or follow-up ended) and competing-risk non-cardiac deaths before the horizon are excluded rather than counted as negatives, since their status at the horizon is unknown. Enrolment dates are not published in this release, so a nominal epoch stands in for the index time - the measured follow-up interval per patient is real, but cross-patient chronological ordering is not recoverable and chronological splitting across patients is therefore not meaningful here; split by patient group instead.
